caveat: Placebo-controlled monotherapy data are old and short-term; ~30-40% do not reach low disease activity (Phase 1)

key_result: SMD -0.49 joints, -0.42 pain; ESR -17.6 mm; withdrawal for adverse reactions OR 3.0
caveat: Effects on overall health status and radiographic progression 'not clear'; higher toxicity withdrawals

key_result: SMDs -0.33 to -0.52 across outcomes
caveat: Weakest csDMARD for disease activity; retained largely for combination use and metabolic/lipid effects

key_result: 78% vs 63% continuing conventional therapy at 1 yr; radiographic change 0.64 (MTX+ETN) vs 0.11 (triple)
caveat: Cheap non-inferior option that is under-used; radiographic difference small and of unclear clinical meaning

outcome: DAS28; Sharp/van der Heijde; adverse events of special interest
key_result: DAS28 0.37 lower (95% CL 0.23, p<0.0001); damage 1.7 points lower (p=0.003); harm 60% vs 49%, adjusted RR 1.24 (95% CL 1.04, p=0.02)
certainty: co-primary benefit and harm both met
caveat: Quantified trade-off rather than a resolution; largest harm contrast was in mostly non-severe infections

intervention: Second-line DMARD choice after b/tsDMARD failure
key_result: Moderate-to-high certainty benefit for an untried TNF inhibitor, IL-6 inhibitors, abatacept, rituximab and JAK inhibitors; untried TNFi OR 6.04 (95% CrI 2.49 to 16.3)
caveat: Establishes that switching works on average but gives no rule for choosing between classes for an individual

key_result: ACR20 38% vs 23% placebo (15% absolute); ACR50 18% vs 7%; ACR70 7% vs 2%; injection-site reactions 71% vs 28%
certainty: authors call it 'clinically meaningful, though modest'
caveat: Statistically positive yet displaced in practice; serious infections 1.8% vs 0.6% (not statistically different). IL-1 is a real but weak axis in RA
Class is licensed in PsA/axSpA but did not enter RA practice. Our search did not retrieve a source documenting the development decision, so the reason is not established here

key_result: Better ACR20 in p38 inhibitor arms but effect not sustained across outcomes
caveat: A mechanistically compelling target with early signal that did not become a drug — a reference case for target-to-drug attrition in RA

key_result: Borderline ACR20 benefit; ACR50 and ACR70 more clearly positive
caveat: Efficacy signal real but modest relative to toxicity (hypertension, diarrhoea); not developed further for RA

key_result: 40% vs 24% placebo (50 mg q4w); and 53.5%/54.8% vs placebo in the larger trial
caveat: Demonstrates that positive phase 3 efficacy does not guarantee approval; the regulatory/safety reasoning was not retrieved by our search
Efficacious but development in RA stopped; drug later succeeded in multiple sclerosis. Shows abandonment can be about risk-benefit context, not target validity

outcome: Erosion healing on HR-pQCT at 24 mo
key_result: Erosion healing 20% (denosumab) vs 6% (placebo), p=0.045
caveat: Does not reduce inflammation or disease activity; addresses the damage-repair unmet need specifically, and is not a DMARD substitute

key_result: ACR20 35.2% (active) vs 24.2% (sham), P=0.0209; open-label 50.0% at 6 mo and 52.8% at 12 mo; related SAEs 1.6%, all perioperative and resolved
caveat: 11-percentage-point separation from sham in a refractory population; open-label figures are not controlled comparisons

key_result: VNS inhibited TNF production for up to 84 days; disease severity improved significantly
caveat: Open-label, no sham; established biological plausibility that RESET-RA later tested

key_result: High-activity cohort DAS28-CRP 4.1 to 3.8 (p=0.02); CRP 8.2 to 6 mg/mL (p=0.01); IFN-gamma 29.8 to 22.5 pg/mL (p=0.02); no effect in low-activity cohort
caveat: 4-day open-label study; a non-invasive route to the same mechanism has not been tested against sham in RA

outcome: Disease activity; B-cell compartment; synovitis imaging
key_result: Rapid decline in disease activity in all 6; depletion of activated memory B cells replaced by IgD+ naive B cells; no clinically relevant cytokine-release syndrome
caveat: n=6, no control; the immune-reset hypothesis it supports is the same one behind CAR-T in autoimmunity

key_result: 49/76 (67%) achieved at least ACR50 at some point after transplant
caveat: Relapse common and procedural mortality non-trivial; largely abandoned in RA once biologics arrived, without a head-to-head comparison

outcome: DAS28, HAQ, ESR/CRP/RF at 1 and 3 yr
key_result: DAS28 and HAQ lower at 1 and 3 yr vs pretreatment (P<0.05); no laboratory abnormalities
caveat: Single-arm; regression to the mean and concomitant DMARDs cannot be separated from the cell effect. Pooled MSC safety across autoimmune indications: AE RR 2.35 (0.58-9.58)

intervention: Regulatory T-cell adoptive transfer; low-dose IL-2
key_result: No controlled RA efficacy data identified in this search
caveat: Tolerance-restoring approaches are the most direct route to drug-free remission (UN3) and have the thinnest RA clinical evidence base of any modern strategy reviewed

key_result: SMD -0.39 (95% CI -0.54 to -0.25); swollen joints -0.08 (-0.22 to -0.07); benefit also on pain, global assessments, ESR
caveat: Genuinely active but slower and weaker than MTX with more toxicity; discontinued on comparative grounds, not on absence of effect
Abandoned for proteinuria, cytopenias and drug-induced autoimmunity rather than lack of efficacy
Efficacy real; malignancy and gonadal toxicity make it indefensible in RA now. Cited here as a negative-by-harm precedent

key_result: Mean BP +5 mmHg at 1-4 mg/kg/d; larger increases above 10 mg/kg/d
caveat: Illustrates a class of effective agents constrained entirely by organ toxicity rather than by efficacy

evidence_base: 99 pts randomised, mean 15.4 yr disease, >5 prior DMARDs
key_result: ITT 28.9% (15/52) column vs 10.6% (5/47) sham, p=0.005; completers 41.7% vs 15.6%
caveat: A genuinely sham-controlled positive result in refractory RA that was dropped for practicality/cost as biologics arrived. Arguably the clearest 'abandoned despite positive evidence' case found

key_result: 7/10 TLI-treated died by 10 yr vs 2/9 chemotherapy; 3 TLI patients developed B-cell malignancies vs 0 controls
caveat: Short-term trials had shown symptomatic benefit. The definitive lesson is about follow-up duration, not about lymphoid targeting

key_result: Meta-analysis OR 4 (95% CI 1.2 to 14) favouring RSO of the knee; the RCT found response 48% in both arms; an earlier review found neither included study favoured yttrium
caveat: A clean example of pooled observational optimism contradicted by randomisation; radiographic damage progressed in 34% of the yttrium arm

verdict_detail: Positive but never replicated at scale
outcome: Multiple joint, pain, laboratory indices at 4 wk and 1 yr
key_result: Significant improvement in tender joints, Ritchie index, swollen joints, pain, morning stiffness, grip strength, ESR, CRP, WBC and HAQ; benefits still present at 1 yr; only pain improved in controls
caveat: Single-blind, residential intervention with an unmatched control setting; the strongest historical dietary result in RA and still the least followed up
Only 4 small RCTs; the claimed certainty grade sits uneasily with that evidence volume and should be checked against the primary trials
An SMD of -2 for a lipid-lowering drug in RA is larger than that of most biologics; I2=97% heterogeneity suggests pooling artefact. Cardiovascular benefit (a separate UN6 goal) is better supported
Conflicts with a negative IV doxycycline RCT (n=23: 1 responder vs 0). Antimicrobial vs anti-MMP mechanism never separated; the infectious-trigger hypothesis behind it remains untested

key_result: Significant reduction in DAS28, ESR and tender joint count vs control
caveat: mTOR inhibition is mechanistically linked to Treg restoration (UN3) but has not been followed up in RA

population: Chronic pain syndromes incl. inflammatory disease
key_result: d = -0.11 (95% CI -0.96 to 0.74), P=0.31 overall; fibromyalgia subgroup d = -0.34 (-0.62 to -0.06); adverse events IRR 1.4 (1.12 to 1.75) vs placebo
caveat: Widely used off-label for RA pain; no RA-specific RCT retrieved. The fibromyalgia signal is relevant because ~34% of RA patients meet fibromyalgia criteria

key_result: Significant improvement in 5 of 7 clinical measures and in ESR; in combination with HCQ only the combination arm improved significantly in all variables
caveat: Positive 1980s-90s data, no modern replication, no mechanism worked out. A genuine dormant lead rather than a refuted one

verdict_detail: Single small positive trial, never followed up
outcome: Pain on movement/at rest, sleep quality, DAS28
key_result: Statistically significant improvements in pain on movement, pain at rest, sleep quality, DAS28 and SF-MPQ present pain; no effect on morning stiffness
caveat: Only controlled cannabinoid trial in RA and it is 20 years old with n=58 over 5 weeks. Directly targets UN2 (pain), which is where the modern pipeline is thinnest

outcome: Patient global impression of change; adverse events
key_result: Superior to placebo for global impression RR 1.44 (95% CI 1.03 to 2.03) but not for withdrawals due to inadequate analgesia; adverse events OR 3.90 (2.31 to 6.56)
caveat: Only strong opioid studied was controlled-release morphine in a single 20-patient trial; trials were 1-6 weeks. The gap between this evidence base and real-world chronic opioid prescribing in RA is large

key_result: No RA-specific controlled trial identified in this search
caveat: Both follow directly from the mucosal-origins hypothesis in Phase 1; neither has an RA efficacy trial. Microbiome-modulating therapies have RCT data only for inflammatory markers, not disease activity
In the 2-yr post-supplementation extension the vitamin D effect disappeared (HR 0.98, 0.83-1.17) while omega-3 became significant (HR 0.83, 0.70-0.99). Outcome is all autoimmune disease, not RA alone

evidence_base: 11 RA studies vs 27 RCTs across autoimmune disease
key_result: One review: DAS-28 WMD -0.83 (95% CI -1.38 to -0.28), p<0.001, 'moderate certainty'; the other: no significant effect on pain scores in RA
caveat: Direct conflict preserved. The positive review reports DAS-28 and ESR benefit but no effect on HAQ or VAS-pain, so the disagreement may be outcome-specific rather than a true contradiction

key_result: TJC SMD -0.59 (95% CI -0.79 to -0.39), P<0.001; ESR, CRP and DAS28 slightly decreased but not statistically significant
caveat: Effect on tender joints without effect on inflammatory markers or composite activity suggests an analgesic rather than disease-modifying action — which is exactly the UN2 target

certainty: 'low quality and small quantity of RCTs'
caveat: Effect size comparable to a biologic from 6 small trials — the classic pattern of small-study bias in supplement literature. Bioavailability of unformulated curcumin is very low
No pooled effect on disease activity or joint counts. Cytokine changes are not a clinical outcome and should not be read as efficacy
Large VAS effect from small trials; selenium has a narrow therapeutic window and toxicity at higher intakes

key_result: Sensitive joints MD -1.66 (95% CI -6.32 to 2.99), I2 93%; swollen joints MD -0.46
caveat: Confidence intervals cross zero on the primary joint outcomes

intervention: Tripterygium wilfordii Hook F, monotherapy vs MTX
key_result: TwHF vs MTX monotherapy: ACR20 RR 1.06 (95% CI 0.90-1.26, moderate certainty); ACR50 RR 1.03 (0.80-1.34, moderate); ACR70 RR 1.12 (0.69-1.79, low)
caveat: Non-inferiority to the anchor drug, not superiority. Trials are almost entirely Chinese, mostly open-label, and TwHF preparations are not standardised

key_result: MTX+TwHF vs MTX: ACR20 RR 1.44 (1.28-1.62, moderate), ACR50 RR 1.88 (1.56-2.28, moderate), ACR70 RR 2.12 (1.40-3.19, low); independent meta: remission rate RR 1.31 (1.11-1.55)
caveat: Efficacy correlated positively with TwHF dose and negatively with MTX dose and with trial risk of bias — the last correlation is a warning that some of the effect is bias

evidence_base: 14 RCTs (AEs) + 40 yr of reproductive toxicity studies
outcome: Infection, liver, renal AEs; reproductive endpoints
key_result: Trials: infection RR 1.37 (0.84-2.23), liver dysfunction RR 1.14 (0.71-1.85), renal damage RR 2.20 (0.50-9.72) — none significant. Toxicology: oligospermia, reduced sperm motility, testicular atrophy, infertility in men; menstrual disorder and amenorrhoea in women
caveat: Short trials in mostly older cohorts cannot detect gonadal toxicity. This is the central unresolved safety question for the best-evidenced TCM intervention in RA

key_result: Added to csDMARDs, TGP improved ACR20, ACR50 and ACR70 response rates and reduced adverse effects versus no add-on
certainty: 'limited methodological quality and strength of evidence'
caveat: The reduction in adverse effects is as interesting as the efficacy claim (a possible MTX-tolerability effect) and is the less-studied of the two

outcome: Improvement rate; morning stiffness; ESR; adverse events
key_result: More improved patients and more RF disappearance than NSAIDs (P<0.00001; P=0.008); better morning stiffness, painful joints and ESR; no difference in swollen joints, grip strength or CRP; fewer digestive but more dermatomucosal adverse events
caveat: NSAIDs are the wrong comparator for a disease-modifying claim; 'RF disappearance' is an unusual endpoint and should be checked in the primary trials

intervention: Iguratimod (synthetic drug of TCM-adjacent origin, licensed in Japan/China)
verdict_detail: Works as add-on; not superior as monotherapy
key_result: IGU+MTX vs MTX: ACR20 RR 1.55 (1.14-2.13), ACR50 RR 2.04 (1.57-2.65), ACR70 RR 2.19 (1.44-3.34), DAS28 WMD -1.65; adverse events no different from MTX alone
caveat: A separate review of 12 trials found monotherapy no better than MTX (ACR20 OR 1.04, 0.79-1.36). Almost unknown outside East Asia despite the largest RCT base of any agent in this table's non-Western group

outcome: DAS28, CRP, ESR, oxidative stress markers
key_result: Improved DAS28 and reduced CRP and ESR across pooled polyphenol interventions
caveat: Pooling 15 chemically unrelated compounds makes the summary estimate hard to interpret or act on

outcome: ESR, CRP, VAS global, swollen/tender joints, DAS
key_result: Cochrane: no statistically significant difference between groups on any measured outcome. CAM review: three sham-controlled trials reported no significant difference in pain reduction
caveat: This is the negative evidence that must be preserved. Both reviews are limited by very small trial numbers, not by trial quality alone

intervention: Electroacupuncture / acupuncture vs conventional therapy and sham (network meta-analysis)
key_result: Electroacupuncture SMD -1.42 (95% CI -1.87 to -0.98); conventional acupuncture SMD -1.11 (-1.49 to -0.73), both vs conventional therapy and non-acupoint sham; SUCRA electroacupuncture 97.7%
caveat: Authors argue same-acupoint sham underestimates the true effect and should not be used as placebo — a claim that, if wrong, would make these effect sizes inflated. The disagreement is about control validity, not about the data

outcome: DAS28, VAS, CRP, ESR, morning stiffness
key_result: Electroacupuncture+DMARDs best for DAS28; fire needle+DMARDs best for VAS, CRP and ESR; moxibustion+DMARDs best for RF; no acupuncture-related therapy beat DMARDs alone for morning stiffness
caveat: All comparisons are open-label add-on versus DMARDs alone, so expectancy and attention effects are unblinded. The negative morning-stiffness result within the same analysis is informative

verdict_detail: Uncertain — large pain effect, tiny trials
key_result: Pain MD -2.15 (95% CI -3.19 to -1.11), 22% absolute improvement (2 studies, 81 pts, very low-quality evidence); DAS-28-ESR reduction 0.40 (95% CI -1.10 to 0.30), inconclusive (1 study, 43 pts)
certainty: very low quality (GRADE), downgraded for imprecision, blinding, attrition
caveat: Majority of trials at high risk of performance and detection bias; ~75% did not report random sequence generation. Pain effect is large but rests on 81 patients

key_result: Mudpacks vs placebo: pain MD 0.50 (95% CI -0.84 to 1.84); tender joints MD -4.60 (-8.72 to -0.48)
caveat: Earlier reviews reported 'most trials positive' with 'weak scientific evidence'; the later Cochrane update with placebo comparison did not confirm pain benefit

key_result: Resistance training: isokinetic strength +23.7% (P<0.001), isometric +35.8% (P<0.001)
caveat: Benefits are on function and strength; no evidence of effect on inflammation or radiographic progression. A low-intensity resistance protocol with blood-flow restriction was null (SMD -0.01)

key_result: Physical activity SMD -0.36 (95% CI -0.62 to -0.10) = 14.4 points lower on a 100-point scale, NNTB 7; psychosocial interventions SMD -0.24 (-0.40 to -0.07), NNTB 10
caveat: The largest evidence base for RA fatigue is non-pharmacological, and the effect is small. No drug has been shown to fix fatigue independently of inflammation

verdict_detail: Works for bone, not for disease activity
key_result: Hip BMD loss smaller with RAPIT: mean decrease 1.6% (95% CI 0.8-2.5) over year 1 and 0.5% over year 2 vs usual care; no difference at lumbar spine
caveat: High-intensity exercise was long avoided in RA on joint-damage grounds; this trial is the main evidence that it is safe as well as useful

key_result: May make little or no difference in pain or disease activity; may slightly increase weight
certainty: low certainty for pain/activity, very low for function
caveat: Conflicts with a pooled analysis of 7 anti-inflammatory-diet RCTs (326 pts) reporting pain -9.22 mm (95% CI -14.15 to -4.29) at very low certainty. Both cannot be strongly true

key_result: Fasting + 13-month vegetarian diet: pain MD -1.89 (95% CI -3.62 to -0.16) on 0-10; 12-wk Cretan Mediterranean diet pain MD -14.00 (-23.6 to -4.37) on 0-100; elemental diet no difference; drop-out 10% higher (RD 0.10, 0.02-0.18) and weight loss 3.23 kg greater in diet arms
caveat: The higher drop-out and weight loss are the most reliably measured findings. Adherence, not efficacy, may be the binding constraint

verdict_detail: Negative overall, positive in a subgroup
key_result: Overall only subjective improvement and no difference between allergen-free and allergen-restricted diets; but 9 patients improved and then flared markedly on rechallenge, with changes in objective activity measures
caveat: One of the few RA studies designed to detect a responder subgroup rather than an average effect. The 'food-intolerant RA' subgroup hypothesis has not been retested with modern tools in 30+ years

evidence_base: 9 studies, 10 comparisons, n=388 (311 for the pooled estimate)
caveat: Directly tests the mucosal-origins hypothesis from Phase 1 by intervention. Selection bias and unstable RA medication were named as heterogeneity sources; authors call for a well-designed prospective trial

evidence_base: 34,101 women, 219 RA cases; 2 intervention studies, 57 pts
outcome: Incident RA; cessation and disease outcomes
key_result: Risk remains elevated 15 yr after cessation (RR 1.99, 95% CI 1.23-3.20) but declines with time since quitting; even 1-7 cigarettes/day RR 2.31 (1.59-3.36). Cessation-intervention trials in RA showed no evidence of benefit
caveat: The gap between a strong causal risk-factor literature and an empty intervention literature is one of the clearest actionable gaps found in this review

verdict_detail: Modest benefit for mood, uncertain for pain
key_result: Pain WMD 0.65 (95% CI -1.11 to -0.18), P=0.006; depression SMD -0.72 (-1.22 to -0.22), P=0.005 in the MBCT analysis
caveat: Effect is clearest on depressed mood rather than on pain or disease activity; unblindable interventions with active-control problems

key_result: Positive across fatigue, balance, QoL and depression, but the pooled evidence is not RA-specific
caveat: RA-specific yoga trials are few and small; most of the supporting evidence is borrowed from other conditions

key_result: No consistent or conclusive evidence
caveat: Sleep disturbance is near-universal in RA and among the least studied modifiable targets
